report.summary: Prop trader bought 1254 at market (10005), then rested three one-sided BUY limits of 4514 each (13542 total, 5.4x depth, 6 ticks from touch) over ~4s. Starting 14s later, the trader sold 1254 at market, filling 700 at 10001-9999. All three bids were cancelled 600 ms after the sell. No fills on the bids, no fills on the same side, cancel symmetry 0. No accepted explanation is supported. The price did not move in the trader's favour (-1.5 ticks, no reversion, round trip -4.77 ticks), so feature (b) is not clearly shown. Feature (a) looks present and the evidence is mixed, so I escalate to Level 2. This is not a STOR draft: there is no repetition and no clear benefit.

response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** ESCALATE, confidence 0.70. Level 2 would draft any STOR. The proposal is recorded as case C-A-261027-0008 and is awaiting a human decision.

**Three facts that drove it:**
1. The trader bought 1254 at market, then rested three one-sided BUY limits of 4514 each. That is 13,542 in total, 5.4x depth, 6 ticks from the touch. None of it executed, and all of it was cancelled 600 ms after the trader's 1254 market SELL, which filled 700 at 10001–9999.
2. No accepted explanation is supported. The trader is a PROP trader with no registered market-making on the instrument, there were no risk events or market events, and cancel_symmetry is 0.
3. Feature (b), a benefit from the opposite-side trade, is not clearly shown. The price moved -1.5 ticks, there was no reversion, and the round trip was -4.77 ticks. There is also no repetition and no prior alert on this trader. That is why I did not propose a STOR draft.

**What would change my mind:** Evidence that the bids were an interrupted genuine attempt to buy, or that the sell was a stop-out of the 1254 long, would support closing. A longer-frame view showing the pattern recurs would support a STOR draft. I only looked at the detector window plus 5 seconds of padding.
